newsitem.title: USA: Phelps Dodge net down on record output.
newsitem.headline: Phelps Dodge net down on record output.

text.p: Phelps Dodge Corp Thursday reported a drop in 1996 profits to $6.97 per share, from $10.65 the previous year, on record copper production.
The 1996 total includes a charge of $0.16 per share.

"In 1996, Phelps Dodge produced a record 1.54 billion pounds of copper, an increase of more than 100 million pounds from the record set in 1995," chief executive Douglas C. Yearley said. "Phelps Dodge Industries also experienced, on an operating basis, record income.
"The copper market, a significant factor in our performance, again surprised many observers," he noted.

"World consumption remained robust and was, from many indications, again at record levels. Prices, although lower and plagued with unusual volatility, proved more resistant to downside pressures than many had anticipated.
"Cash flow provided by operating activities, the principal measure of our operating performance, was $837.5 million in 1996, compared with $959.0 million in 1995.

"This included 1996 cash flow of $649.0 million from Phelps Dodge Mining Co despite the lower average copper prices and record 1996 cash flow of $238.9 million from Phelps Dodge Industries," Yearley said.

Last year's sales were $3.79 billion, compared with $4.19 billion in 1995, Phelps Dodge said, explaining the decrease was primarily a result of lower average copper prices and lower sales volumes of wheels and rims.
The decrease was partially offset by higher sales volumes of copper, specialty chemicals and wire and cable products.

As of December 31, the company said, it had net hedge positions in place with financial institutions that provide for a minimum 1997 first quarter average price of $0.90 per pound for 85 million pounds of copper cathode.
These minimum prices are based on average London Metal Exchange prices, it noted.

Contracts ensuring minimum prices for 185 million pounds of 1996 third quarter copper production resulted in payments of $3.1 million to Phelps Dodge. Similar contracts covering 695 million pounds of 1996 copper production expired without payment.

During the 1996 third quarter, the company liquidated a portion of its copper price protection contracts that covered anticipated production in the fourth quarter of 1996 and the first quarter of 1997.

This resulted in cash payments to the company of $15.6 million. Consequently, $8.8 million for the 1996 fourth quarter contract was recognized in income during the fourth quarter and $6.8 million for the 1997 first quarter contract was deferred and will be recognized in income during the 1997 first quarter. ((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.))
